title: Refuter reply
description: What a legal-refuter seat returns, as it returns it: a JSON array holding one object per candidate it was handed (product/plugin/agents/legal-refuter.md, section 'Output - the JSON array, and nothing else'). `verdict-capture` checks a reply against this schema before it writes the reply's bytes, unchanged, to .legal/verdicts/refutation/. Before this file no schema described the reply: verdict.schema.json's `refutation` object is the MERGED form, with no `finding_id` and no `confidence`, and `additionalProperties: false`, so the reply the refuter's own definition asks for failed it by construction. Every field here refers to the definition verdict.schema.json already gives it; the required list and the rule on `grounds` are the Output section's.
$comment: Relay unit `capture`, 2026-09-24. `grounds`: the Output section says 'omit unless overturned', and SKILL.md step 5 keeps an overturn's grounds as the reason for the dismissal, so an overturn carries them and nothing else does. The `reading` block is verdict.schema.json's `$defs.refutationReading`, the node the log keeps it under: until then this file built its own copy of the rows from verdict.schema.json's row properties while the log held another, the two drifted apart when relay item 6 gave the refuter `disposition`, `cover_ground` and a covered row's `ground`, and live run 2's report was refused for it. Tightened the same day: an `overturned` outcome carries at least one `evidence` entry, which is a quotation (Rules, 1: 'Quote real source for every conclusion, in both directions. An overturn with no quote is an opinion'); a row's `disposition` is one of the seat's four words, not `not_read`, and a `searched` row is the seat's row without the replay's `hit_hash` (both now verdict.schema.json's `$defs`, `seatDisposition` and `seatSearchRow`).

items.$comment: (design-not-violations.md sections 2.4 and 2.5 item 5) An entry that carries `mode` is the second look's reply, `$defs.challengeItem`; every other entry is the ordinary pass's, the `else` branch, accepted or refused exactly as before. A reply in challenge mode carries no `decisions`, no `searched` and none of the seven ordinary grounds; an ordinary one carries no `mode`.

decisions.description: Present only where the candidate carried `kinds`, and optional there: the refuter's reading is a record, not a duty. One decision per unit or sub-shape it opened, keyed by the ids the census gives (adjudicator-reply.schema.json's `decision`: `unit`, `quote`, `ground`, and where they apply `disposition`, `also`, `rest`, `at`), or units it chose not to open under one note. `verdict-capture` writes the refutation's `reading` block from them (verdict.schema.json's `refutationReading`: `read`, `covered`, `not_read`), recording every unit the refuter did not name as not read by it; a reply carrying `reading` is refused naming this form.

searched.description: Every project-wide search the refuter ran, as the refutation's `reading.searched[]` rows. Present only where the candidate carried `kinds`.

challengeItem.$comment: THE SECOND LOOK'S REPLY, taken by `items` for an entry that carries `mode`. A challenge seat tries to show that a finding the report does not count is one to fix after all: the duty is not met, the exemption does not apply, the file ships, or (`applies-after-all`, a high finding the first review ruled out, in a run with the second check) the rule applies after all. The assembly applies its outcome to the finding's placement (`disposition.ts`), never to its verdict: `overturned` puts it back among those to fix, `needs_human` leaves it to the person, `upheld` keeps it where the first review put it.
